papers.title: An Accurate and Efficient Approach to Knowledge Extraction from Scientific Publications Using Structured Ontology Models, Graph Neural Networks, and Large Language Models
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of biomedical literature makes it challenging for researchers to stay current. Integrating knowledge from various sources is crucial for studying complex biological systems. Traditional text-mining methods often have limited accuracy because they don’t capture semantic and contextual nuances. Deep-learning models can be computationally expensive and typically have low interpretability, though efforts in explainable AI aim to mitigate this. Furthermore, transformer-based models have a tendency to produce false or made-up information—a problem known as hallucination—which is especially prevalent in large language models (LLMs). This study proposes a hybrid approach combining text-mining techniques with graph neural networks (GNNs) and fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) to extend biomedical knowledge graphs and interpret predicted edges based on published literature. An LLM is used to validate predictions and provide explanations. Evaluated on a corpus of experimentally confirmed protein interactions, the approach achieved a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) of 0.772. Applied to insomnia, the approach identified 25 interactions between 32 human proteins absent in known knowledge bases, including regulatory interactions between MAOA and 5-HT2C, binding between ADAM22 and 14-3-3 proteins, which is implicated in neurological diseases, and a circadian regulatory loop involving RORB and NR1D1. The hybrid GNN-LLM method analyzes biomedical literature efficiency to uncover potential molecular interactions for complex disorders. It can accelerate therapeutic target discovery by focusing expert verification on the most relevant automatically extracted information.

papers.title: AI Agent-Driven Framework for Automated Product Knowledge Graph Construction in E-Commerce
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of e-commerce platforms generates vast amounts of unstructured product data, creating significant challenges for information retrieval, recommendation systems, and data analytics. Knowledge Graphs (KGs) offer a structured, interpretable format to organize such data, yet constructing product-specific KGs remains a complex and manual process. This paper introduces a fully automated, AI agent-driven framework for constructing product knowledge graphs directly from unstructured product descriptions. Leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs), our method operates in three stages using dedicated agents: ontology creation and expansion, ontology refinement, and knowledge graph population. This agent-based approach ensures semantic coherence, scalability, and high-quality output without relying on predefined schemas or handcrafted extraction rules. We evaluate the system on a real-world dataset of air conditioner product descriptions, demonstrating strong performance in both ontology generation and KG population. The framework achieves over 97\% property coverage and minimal redundancy, validating its effectiveness and practical applicability. Our work highlights the potential of LLMs to automate structured knowledge extraction in retail, providing a scalable path toward intelligent product data integration and utilization.

papers.title: Hierarchical Attentional Hybrid Neural Networks for Document Classification
papers.abstract: Document classification is a challenging task with important applications. The deep learning approaches to the problem have gained much attention recently. Despite the progress, the proposed models do not incorporate the knowledge of the document structure in the architecture efficiently and not take into account the contexting importance of words and sentences. In this paper, we propose a new approach based on a combination of convolutional neural networks, gated recurrent units, and attention mechanisms for document classification tasks. The main contribution of this work is the use of convolution layers to extract more meaningful, generalizable and abstract features by the hierarchical representation. The proposed method in this paper improves the results of the current attention-based approaches for document classification.

papers.title: Combining machine learning, simulations and experiments for improved glass design
papers.abstract: The design of novel glasses with tailored properties remains a grand challenge in materials science, traditionally requiring extensive trial-and-error experimentation. This talk presents a comprehensive framework that integrates machine learning, atomistic simulations, and targeted experiments to accelerate the discovery and optimization of glass compositions. We demonstrate how large-scale machine learning models trained on experimental databases can predict glass properties across nearly the entire periodic table, enabling rapid screening of promising compositions. These predictions are refined through physics-informed graph neural networks that capture atomic-scale interactions and energy conservation principles, providing deeper insights into structure-property relationships. The framework is enhanced by automated knowledge extraction from scientific literature using our materials-specific language model (MatSciBERT) and natural language processing techniques. We showcase practical applications including the development of radiation-resistant nuclear waste glasses, scratch-resistant display glasses, and specialty glasses for space applications. The talk concludes by highlighting how this integrated approach has led to the discovery of novel glass compositions with superior properties, validated through experimental synthesis and characterization. Our results demonstrate that the synergistic combination of artificial intelligence, computational modeling, and experimental validation can significantly accelerate the glass design process while reducing resource requirements and environmental impact.

papers.title: The Deep Arbitrary Polynomial Chaos Neural Network or how Deep Artificial Neural Networks could benefit from Data-Driven Homogeneous Chaos Theory
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence and Machine learning have been widely used in various fields of mathematical computing, physical modeling, computational science, communication science, and stochastic analysis. Approaches based on Deep Artificial Neural Networks (DANN) are very popular in our days. Depending on the learning task, the exact form of DANNs is determined via their multi-layer architecture, activation functions and the so-called loss function. However, for a majority of deep learning approaches based on DANNs, the kernel structure of neural signal processing remains the same, where the node response is encoded as a linear superposition of neural activity, while the non-linearity is triggered by the activation functions. In the current paper, we suggest to analyze the neural signal processing in DANNs from the point of view of homogeneous chaos theory as known from polynomial chaos expansion (PCE). From the PCE perspective, the (linear) response on each node of a DANN could be seen as a $1^{st}$ degree multi-variate polynomial of single neurons from the previous layer, i.e. linear weighted sum of monomials. From this point of view, the conventional DANN structure relies implicitly (but erroneously) on a Gaussian distribution of neural signals. Additionally, this view revels that by design DANNs do not necessarily fulfill any orthogonality or orthonormality condition for a majority of data-driven applications. Therefore, the prevailing handling of neural signals in DANNs could lead to redundant representation as any neural signal could contain some partial information from other neural signals. To tackle that challenge, we suggest to employ the data-driven generalization of PCE theory known as arbitrary polynomial chaos (aPC) to construct a corresponding multi-variate orthonormal representations on each node of a DANN to obtain Deep arbitrary polynomial chaos neural networks.

literature_themes.theme: Advancements in Graph Neural Networks and Knowledge Extraction Techniques
literature_themes.summary: This cluster of papers explores the integration of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) with various AI methodologies, including Large Language Models (LLMs), to enhance knowledge extraction from complex datasets such as biomedical literature and e-commerce product descriptions. The studies propose innovative frameworks for constructing knowledge graphs and improving document classification, emphasizing the importance of semantic coherence and interpretability in AI-driven approaches.
literature_themes.limitations: Many papers lack detailed abstracts, limiting the understanding of their contributions. Additionally, challenges such as the computational expense of deep learning models, low interpretability, and issues like hallucination in LLMs remain prevalent. The effectiveness of the proposed methods needs further validation across diverse datasets and applications.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster highlights the need for more efficient and interpretable AI techniques in knowledge extraction and graph construction, addressing gaps in current methodologies. By combining GNNs with LLMs and focusing on automated processes, the research supports the identification of new avenues for improving knowledge representation and retrieval in various domains.

literature_themes.theme: Integrating Machine Learning and Simulations in Glass Design
literature_themes.summary: This cluster focuses on the development of a comprehensive framework that combines machine learning, atomistic simulations, and experimental approaches to enhance the design and optimization of glass materials. It highlights the use of large-scale machine learning models for predicting glass properties and refining these predictions through advanced neural networks, ultimately leading to practical applications in various specialized glass types.
literature_themes.limitations: The framework's reliance on existing experimental databases may limit its applicability to novel glass compositions not well-represented in the data. Additionally, the complexity of atomic-scale interactions may still pose challenges in accurately predicting properties for all glass types.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster identifies a significant research gap in the integration of computational and experimental methods in materials science, particularly in the context of glass design. It supports further exploration into the development of more generalized models and the expansion of databases to include a wider variety of glass compositions.

literature_themes.theme: Deep Learning and Chaos Theory Integration
literature_themes.summary: This cluster explores the intersection of Deep Artificial Neural Networks (DANN) and homogeneous chaos theory, particularly how polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) can enhance the understanding and structure of DANNs. The papers suggest that viewing neural signal processing through the lens of chaos theory can provide new insights into the architecture and functioning of DANNs, potentially leading to improved performance in various applications.
literature_themes.limitations: The cluster primarily focuses on theoretical frameworks and lacks extensive empirical validation of the proposed methodologies. Additionally, the practical implementation of chaos theory concepts in existing DANN architectures remains underexplored.
literature_themes.gap_relevance: This cluster highlights a significant gap in the integration of chaos theory with deep learning, suggesting that further research could lead to innovative approaches in neural network design and optimization, thereby addressing current limitations in DANN performance.

summary: The literature on Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for large-scale knowledge discovery emphasizes advancements in integrating GNNs with AI methodologies like Large Language Models (LLMs) to enhance knowledge extraction from complex datasets. Key themes include the need for improved interpretability and efficiency in knowledge representation, the potential of GNNs in automating knowledge graph construction, and the exploration of novel theoretical frameworks such as hyperbolic GNNs and chaos theory integration. However, gaps remain in empirical validation across diverse applications and the generalizability of proposed methods beyond specific domains.
scholarly_positioning: While prior research has made significant strides in integrating Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) with Large Language Models (LLMs) for knowledge extraction, many approaches remain constrained by limited empirical validation and domain specificity, particularly in biomedical literature. Existing methodologies often overlook the complexities of diverse scientific datasets and fail to provide interpretable frameworks that enhance knowledge representation. Furthermore, the theoretical explorations of hyperbolic GNNs and chaos theory integration have not been sufficiently operationalized in practical applications, leaving a gap in understanding their potential for large-scale knowledge discovery. This proposed research aims to address these limitations by developing a robust, empirically validated framework that leverages GNNs for automated knowledge graph construction across varied scientific domains, thereby contributing to a more nuanced understanding of knowledge extraction processes in literature.
research_scope: This study will focus on the application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for automated knowledge graph construction in the domain of biomedical literature. The primary objective is to develop a hybrid framework that integrates GNNs with Large Language Models (LLMs) to enhance knowledge extraction from diverse scientific datasets over a six-month evaluation period. The research will compare the proposed GNN-LLM framework against traditional GNN methods and existing knowledge extraction techniques, using metrics such as accuracy, F1-score, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) as primary outcomes. Secondary outcomes will include the interpretability of the knowledge graphs generated and the property coverage achieved in the knowledge representation. This study aims to empirically validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach across multiple biomedical datasets, addressing the gap in generalizability and interpretability in current methodologies.

{
  "Graph Neural Networks (GNNs)": "A type of neural network designed to process data structured as graphs, enabling the extraction of relationships and features from nodes and edges in a graph.",
  "Large Language Models (LLMs)": "Advanced neural network models trained on vast text corpora to understand and generate human-like text, used here to enhance knowledge extraction.",
  "Knowledge Graph Construction": "The process of creating a structured representation of knowledge, where entities are nodes and relationships are edges, facilitating easier access and understanding of information.",
  "Accuracy": "A metric measuring the proportion of true positive and true negative predictions among the total number of cases evaluated.",
  "F1-score": "A metric that combines precision and recall to provide a single score that balances both, particularly useful in imbalanced datasets.",
  "Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC)": "A metric that provides a balanced measure of the quality of binary classifications, taking into account true and false positives and negatives.",
  "Interpretability": "The degree to which a human can understand the cause of a decision made by a model, often assessed through methods like output-level explanations or representation-level comparisons.",
  "Output-level Explanation": "An interpretability method that explains the final predictions of a model in human-understandable terms.",
  "Representation-level Comparisons": "An interpretability method that analyzes and compares the internal representations learned by the model to understand its decision-making process.",
  "Diverse Datasets": "A collection of datasets from various sources and domains, ensuring that the model is tested on a wide range of scenarios to validate its generalizability.",

    "Blind Trust": "A scenario where users rely on a model without understanding its limitations or decision-making processes.",
    "Perceived Transparency": "How clearly a model communicates its processes and decisions to users, impacting their trust.",

technical_feasibility: The proposed study requires access to open-source models for GNNs and LLMs to facilitate hidden state extraction and internal representation analysis. It also necessitates labeled datasets from biomedical literature for training and evaluation, as well as GPU resources for model training and evaluation. If only API models are available, the design should be revised to focus on output-level explanations or black-box evaluations. Additionally, if user trust is investigated, a human-subject design will be essential, requiring ethics approval and measures for trust calibration. To address potential gaps, the study could consider using publicly available datasets and existing open-source GNN and LLM frameworks to ensure feasibility.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) in knowledge extraction from biomedical literature; however, they treat the integration of diverse scientific datasets and the interpretability of knowledge graphs as secondary, leaving unclear whether the proposed frameworks can generalize across different domains and enhance user understanding. This matters practically because improved interpretability and generalizability can significantly impact the usability of knowledge extraction tools in various scientific fields; therefore, this study investigates the integration of GNNs with Large Language Models (LLMs) for automated knowledge graph construction across multiple scientific domains, focusing on empirical validation and interpretability.
question: How does the integration of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) with Large Language Models (LLMs) improve the accuracy and interpretability of automated knowledge graph construction in biomedical literature compared to traditional GNN methods?
theoretical_mechanism: The proposed research investigates the integration of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) with Large Language Models (LLMs) to enhance the accuracy and interpretability of automated knowledge graph construction in biomedical literature. The independent variable is the GNN-LLM integration, which serves as a mediator through improved representation features that facilitate knowledge extraction. The dependent variable is the accuracy and interpretability of the knowledge graphs generated. The theoretical framework is grounded in knowledge representation theories, with the causal chain indicating that enhanced representation features lead to better knowledge extraction outcomes. System-level outcomes, such as unsafe response rates, are mediated by technical mechanisms like safety detection and filters, while user-level outcomes, including trust and satisfaction, are mediated by psychological mechanisms such as perceived transparency. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of representation features in improving knowledge extraction and the impact of perceived transparency on user trust and satisfaction.
hypothesis: The integration of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) with Large Language Models (LLMs) will significantly improve the accuracy of automated knowledge graph construction in biomedical literature compared to traditional GNN methods, mediated by enhanced representation features that facilitate knowledge extraction.

proposal: This research proposal aims to develop a hybrid framework integrating Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) with Large Language Models (LLMs) to enhance automated knowledge graph construction in biomedical literature, addressing the significant gap in empirical validation of GNN-LLM integration across diverse scientific datasets and its impact on user interpretability. The study will operationalize key concepts such as GNNs as neural networks for graph-structured data, LLMs for text understanding, and knowledge graph construction as the process of creating structured knowledge representations. Technical feasibility is ensured through access to open-source models and labeled biomedical datasets, with contingency plans for resource limitations. The motivation stems from the need for improved accuracy and interpretability in knowledge extraction tools, as existing methodologies often overlook the complexities of diverse datasets and user understanding. Scholarly positioning highlights unresolved tensions in the literature regarding the generalizability of GNN applications beyond biomedical contexts. The research question investigates how GNN-LLM integration improves accuracy and interpretability in knowledge graph construction compared to traditional GNN methods. The theoretical mechanism posits that enhanced representation features from GNN-LLM integration (independent variable) lead to improved accuracy and interpretability of knowledge graphs (dependent variables), with system-level outcomes mediated by technical mechanisms and user-level outcomes influenced by perceived transparency. The falsifiable hypothesis states that GNN-LLM integration will significantly enhance accuracy in knowledge graph construction. Constructs will be operationalized using metrics such as accuracy, F1-score, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC) for knowledge graphs, alongside interpretability measures through output-level explanations. The methodology will employ a comparative analysis against traditional GNN methods, utilizing diverse biomedical datasets and rigorous evaluation metrics, with controls for dataset variability and statistical analysis to ensure validity. Expected contributions include theoretical advancements in knowledge representation, technical innovations in interpretability methods, empirical validation of GNN-LLM frameworks, and practical guidelines for deploying knowledge extraction tools. Key limitations include potential data sparsity, model overfitting, and challenges in user trust, which will be mitigated through diverse datasets, regularization techniques, and user studies.

rubric_scores.level: 12-13: strong and clear research framing with minor conceptual weaknesses
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal clearly defines the research problem of enhancing knowledge graph construction using GNNs and LLMs, but lacks precise operational definitions for key concepts like 'interpretability' and 'accuracy' in the context of knowledge graphs. Major weaknesses: Key concepts are not fully operationalized, leading to potential ambiguity in understanding the research boundaries and implications. Next band requirements: To move into the next band, the proposal needs to provide explicit definitions and operationalization of all key constructs, ensuring clarity in how they relate to the research problem.

rubric_scores.level: 9-11: generally connected but some weak transitions or unsupported assumptions
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal presents a logical flow from the problem to the hypothesis, but lacks strong justification for the causal claims regarding the GNN-LLM integration's impact on accuracy and interpretability. Major weaknesses: Causal claims are not sufficiently supported by empirical evidence or theoretical backing, leading to potential gaps in reasoning. Next band requirements: To achieve a higher score, the proposal must strengthen the justification for causal claims and ensure that all components of the research are tightly interconnected with robust theoretical support.

The proposal introduces a hybrid framework combining GNNs and LLMs, which is a relevant contribution; however, it primarily builds on existing methodologies without presenting a significantly new theoretical framework or mechanism. Major weaknesses: The novelty is somewhat limited as it does not clearly differentiate itself from existing works that also integrate GNNs with LLMs. Next band requirements: To elevate the score, the proposal should articulate a unique theoretical contribution or framework that advances the understanding of knowledge extraction beyond existing literature.

The methodology is generally sound, with a clear plan for empirical validation; however, it lacks detailed descriptions of controls and potential confounding factors. Major weaknesses: Insufficient detail on how confounding variables will be managed and the robustness of evaluation metrics. Next band requirements: To improve, the proposal must include comprehensive details on experimental controls, confound handling, and a more robust evaluation design.

rubric_scores.level: 9-11: relevant literature used but somewhat surface-level
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal references relevant literature but does not engage deeply with competing approaches or critically analyze the limitations of existing work. Major weaknesses: Lacks a thorough comparative analysis of methodologies and does not sufficiently identify unresolved tensions in the literature. Next band requirements: To achieve a higher score, the proposal should provide a critical synthesis of the literature, identifying specific gaps and how this research addresses them.

rubric_scores.level: 7-8: approaching PhD-level with some shallow areas
rubric_scores.justification: The proposal demonstrates some theoretical depth but lacks comprehensive discussion of the mechanisms underlying the proposed integration and its implications. Major weaknesses: Insufficient exploration of the theoretical mechanisms and limitations, which are crucial for PhD-level work. Next band requirements: To improve, the proposal should delve deeper into the theoretical underpinnings of the research and discuss potential limitations and trade-offs.

The writing is generally clear and organized, but some areas lack precision and conciseness. Major weaknesses: Certain sections could benefit from more concise language and clearer terminology. Next band requirements: To reach a higher score, the proposal should refine its language for greater clarity and precision.

Final verdict: The proposal demonstrates potential but lacks the depth and rigor expected for PhD-level research maturity.
